notes: Saint John heads a section two ways - '4.2(5) PARKING LOT STANDARDS' and '5.2 Fences' - and only the first was once recognised. Everything under a title-case heading merged upward, so a single clause ran from parking standards to signs thirty pages later. expect_sections here is mostly title-case headings for that reason: they fail if that regresses.

This consolidation carries the 2025 merger of the R1, R2 and RSS zones into Low-Rise Residential (RL), which is the amendment the registry flags as the highest staleness consequence in the set. The rl-zone-exists question fails if the source is ever replaced with a pre-2025 copy.
Definitions are unnumbered and alphabetical, so they are cited under section 3.1 with the defined term as the heading rather than by position.

questions.question: What is a secondary suite?
questions.why: Definitions chapter. 370 definitions were once cited as section 0(N), which this bylaw has no such thing as.

questions.question: What residential zones are there in Saint John?
questions.why: Pins document currency. A pre-2025 consolidation answers this with R1 and R2 zones that no longer exist.

questions.question: How tall can I build a fence in my back yard?
questions.why: A title-case heading. Until both heading forms were recognised, this section had no clause of its own and its text sat inside a parking provision.

questions.question: When do I have to provide bicycle parking?
questions.why: Another title-case heading, and the thresholds are the kind of number an answer must not invent.

questions.question: Does a parking lot have to be paved?
questions.why: The clause that was 42,672 characters long. It must now hold parking lot standards and nothing else.
